features.title: Migration script: drop Medusa global unique constraints blocking multi-vendor
features.user_visible_behavior: Two or more sellers can create fulfillment sets, shipping profiles, and service zones with the same name (e.g. "Standard Delivery", "US Domestic") without the second creation failing with a unique constraint violation.
verification: 1. Spin up a fresh DB and run all Medusa + Mercur migrations.

2. Run `bunx medusa db:migrate:scripts` from the project (apps/api). Medusa auto-discovers every plugin's `<plugin.resolve>/migration-scripts/*.js` and tracks executed runs in `script_migrations` so it runs once per project. `@mercurjs/core` ships the script under `.medusa/server/src/migration-scripts/`.
3. Verify the three partial unique indexes are gone:
- IDX_fulfillment_set_name_unique
- IDX_shipping_profile_name_unique
- IDX_service_zone_name_unique
Query: SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE indexname IN ('IDX_fulfillment_set_name_unique','IDX_shipping_profile_name_unique','IDX_service_zone_name_unique'); — must return 0 rows.

4. Integration test: create two sellers, have each create a fulfillment set named "Standard Delivery", a shipping profile named "Standard Delivery", and a service zone named "US Domestic". Both must succeed. Covered by `integration-tests/http/migrations/drop-fulfillment-global-unique-indexes.spec.ts`.
5. Re-running the script must be idempotent (uses DROP INDEX IF EXISTS). Covered by the same spec.

evidence.auto_discovery: Confirmed in /Users/viktorholik/Desktop/medusa/packages/medusa/src/commands/db/run-scripts.ts:52-55 — `scriptsSourcePaths` includes `join(plugin.resolve, "migration-scripts")` for every loaded plugin. Plugin `resolve` is `<pkg>/.medusa/server/src/` per /Users/viktorholik/Desktop/medusa/packages/core/utils/src/common/get-resolved-plugins.ts:86. Tracking table is `script_migrations` so each script runs at most once per project.
evidence.test_strategy: Test does not import the migration script directly. It instantiates Medusa's `MigrationScriptsMigrator` and points it at `<@mercurjs/core>/.medusa/server/src/migration-scripts/` (resolved via `require.resolve('@mercurjs/core/package.json')`). That is the same discovery path Medusa walks in `db:migrate:scripts`, so the test verifies the script is wired in through plugin auto-attach.
evidence.test_run_pending: Run via `bun run test:integration:http -- migrations/drop-fulfillment-global-unique-indexes` after `bun run build`. Requires Postgres + Redis.

features.notes:
Constraint sources in the Medusa codebase (/Users/viktorholik/Desktop/medusa):
- medusa/packages/modules/fulfillment/src/migrations/Migration20240311145700_InitialSetupMigration.ts:48 → IDX_fulfillment_set_name_unique on (name) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
- same migration L58 → IDX_service_zone_name_unique on (name) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
- same migration L103 → IDX_shipping_profile_name_unique on (name) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

Impact: every seller creates these resources during onboarding. Common names collide on the second seller — day-one blocker for any marketplace with >1 seller. Customers never see these names, so dropping the global uniqueness is safe.

Implementation:
- `packages/core/src/migration-scripts/drop-fulfillment-global-unique-indexes.ts` — single transaction issuing three `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS` statements via the PG_CONNECTION knex instance.
- No module-install gate is needed: the fulfillment module is always installed in a Mercur marketplace, and `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS` no-ops on missing indexes.
- Mounted automatically because Medusa's `db:migrate:scripts` walks `join(plugin.resolve, "migration-scripts")` for each plugin — the file lives at `packages/core/src/migration-scripts/` and compiles to the corresponding location under `.medusa/server/src/`.

Application-layer workaround already used: auto-prefix names with seller handle/ID. This migration removes the need for that workaround at the DB level.

features.title: sms.ir transport client + Medusa SMS notification provider
features.user_visible_behavior: The platform can deliver SMS through sms.ir: high-priority OTP messages via POST /v1/send/verify, and general transactional messages via the standard send endpoint. With no SMSIR_API_KEY set, sends are logged in dev instead of failing.
verification: 1. Set SMSIR_API_KEY (+ optional SMSIR_BASE_URL). Without it, `send`/`sendVerify` log a dev payload and no-op.
2. Unit test smsirClient: X-API-KEY header, correct base URL, verify body shape { mobile, templateId, parameters:[{name,value}] }.
3. Notification provider registered on channel 'sms' via withMercur; createNotifications({channel:'sms', data:{templateId, params}}) reaches smsirClient (mock transport).
4. `bun run build` green.

evidence.source: packages/core/src/providers/smsir/client.ts (transport, X-API-KEY, sendVerify, dev no-op when no key); packages/core/src/providers/notification-smsir/{service,index}.ts (AbstractNotificationProviderService, channel sms, ModuleProvider(Modules.NOTIFICATION)).

features.notes: Design: docs/features/phone-auth-and-notifications.md §3-§5. Shared transport at packages/core/src/providers/smsir/client.ts is used by BOTH the notification provider (transactional) and the OTP path (auth) — but only the transport is shared; the pathways are separate. Provider structure mirrors packages/providers/payout-stripe-connect/src. Only SMSIR_API_KEY lives in env; all template ids live in DB.

features.title: Passwordless phone (OTP) auth provider + OTP module (customer + vendor)
features.user_visible_behavior: A customer (storefront) or vendor (member) can register/log in with a phone number: request an OTP, receive it by SMS, enter it, and get an authenticated session. Email + password login keeps working unchanged. Phone is the primary, unique identity; email is optional.
verification: 1. POST /vendor/auth/phone/request-otp { phone } → 200, an OtpCode row is created, smsirClient.sendVerify called (mock).
2. POST /vendor/auth/phone/verify-otp { phone, code } → session token; wrong/expired/over-attempt code → 401 and attempts increments.
3. First-time verify creates auth_identity (providerIdentity.entity_id = phone); subsequent vendor seller creation runs on that auth_identity_id (createSellerAccountWorkflow).
4. Same for /store/auth/phone/* creating a customer with phone.
5. Phone uniqueness enforced; existing emailpass login path still passes.
6. OTP isolation: changing notification-settings does NOT affect OTP delivery.
7. Integration tests under integration-tests/http/auth/... with sms.ir client mocked; `bun run build` green.

features.title: Notification pipeline: hybrid event catalog + settings module + sendNotificationWorkflow + orchestrator
features.user_visible_behavior: Domain events (order placed, payout, return, seller approved, ...) are delivered to recipients over the channel(s) the operator configured, with retry/idempotency. No subscriber calls the notification module directly.
verification: 1. registerNotificationEvent() builds a hybrid catalog; effective catalog = static registry left-joined with DB NotificationChannelConfig (defaults created on first read).
2. Single orchestrator subscriber binds config.event = catalog.eventKeys(), builds a NotificationIntent, runs sendNotificationWorkflow.
3. Pipeline steps: resolveRecipients (fan-out N), applyPolicy (enabled + capability + template-gate), buildTemplate (email render / sms param-map), routeChannels, dispatch (Modules.NOTIFICATION).
4. Tests: event with channel=email → only email; channel=sms → only sms; recipient without phone → sms dropped (fallback/skip); duplicate dedupe_key → no resend; sms without template_id → not sent.
5. `bun run build` + integration suites green.

features.notes: Design: docs/features/phone-auth-and-notifications.md §3, §4, §6, §7. Dispatch sits on top of Modules.NOTIFICATION (gives feed channel free). Policy is a thin pure function — quiet-hours/rate/per-user prefs intentionally out of v1 scope but attach here. Catalog includes a read-only `system` row for OTP (display only; not routed).

features.title: Admin page: per-event channel (email/SMS) configuration
features.user_visible_behavior: In the admin panel, an operator sees every notification event grouped by audience and, per event, toggles Email and SMS and enters the approved sms.ir template_id. SMS stays disabled with a hint until a template_id is provided. The OTP row is shown read-only/system.
verification: 1. GET /admin/notification-settings returns the merged effective catalog (RBAC-protected).
2. POST persists per (event_key, channel): enabled + template_id; SMS cannot be enabled without a template_id.

3. UI (packages/admin/src/pages/notification-settings) follows admin-page-ui / admin-form-ui / admin-ui-review skills: Form.Field, i18n keys, data-testid, correct heading levels; route+nav registered via get-route-map.tsx.
4. Setting a template_id and enabling SMS routes a triggered event over SMS (feed/log evidence); disabling it does not affect OTP.
5. `bun run lint` + `bun run build` green; client route map regenerated via mercurjs codegen.
